Allegorical

al-uh-GOR-ih-kul -- from allegory ('a story with a hidden symbolic meaning') + -ical. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

To be allegorical is to be symbolic with hidden meaning.

The teacher explained that the story of the tortoise and the hare is allegorical, using animals to symbolize the dangers of overconfidence.

Worked Example

Animal Farm is a famous allegorical book -- on the surface, it's about farm animals overthrowing their farmer, but every character actually represents a real figure or idea from the Russian Revolution.

Allegorical works always operate on two levels at once -- a literal surface story and a hidden symbolic meaning underneath; the skill is being able to read both layers.

How Allegorical Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

symbolic

symbolic: representing something else through symbols

metaphorical

metaphorical: using an image or idea to mean something beyond its literal sense

Antonyms

literal

literal: true to the exact, factual meaning of the words

factual

factual: concerned only with plain facts, not hidden meaning

How Strong Is It? — symbolic → allegorical → metaphorical

symbolic vs. allegorical

symbolic vs. allegorical: Symbolic describes a single image or object representing an idea -- a dove symbolizes peace.

metaphorical vs. allegorical

metaphorical vs. allegorical: Metaphorical is the broadest term, covering any language or image that isn't meant literally, without necessarily building a whole hidden story the way allegorical does.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of allegorical.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — allegor-

root — allegor-: a story with a hidden symbolic meaning (Greek allos 'other' + agoreuein 'to speak')

suffix — -ical

suffix — -ical: having the qualities of; pertaining to

Put it together

Put it together: Allegorical comes from allegory -- Greek allos ('other') plus agoreuein ('to speak'), literally 'other-speaking' -- plus -ical. An allegorical story always says one thing on the surface while 'speaking other' meanings underneath.

Use the root in a new word: allegory

Use the root in a new word: allegory: Plato's famous allegory of the cave describes prisoners who mistake shadows on a wall for reality.

Root Check

Word Choice

Allegorical works best for stories, poems, or artworks built with an intentional hidden layer of meaning throughout -- don't use it loosely for something that's simply 'symbolic' in one small, one-off way.
